claim: A frequency byte does not drive a formula and does not have a hundred and twenty-eight values. Its top four bits index a table of sixteen entries, so eight settings share each entry, and the entries are the named third octaves between the two frequencies the page prints against that address. On 200 - 6.3k that is 200, 250, 315, 400, 500, 630, 800, 1k, 1.25k, 1.6k, 2k, 2.5k, 3.15k, 4k, 5k, 6.3k. Rendered through the same bands the takes were read in, the model's peak lands in exactly the unit's band at every setting from 32 up -- 7 of 12 at one address and both of the two at the other -- and read again by a fit over the whole feature the two are 0.013 to 0.047 octaves apart there, which is a fifth of a band. It does not hold at the bottom: the three entries below 315 Hz read 0.06 to 0.17 octaves below where the named series puts them, at settings 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, repeatably, at both addresses, at two band widths and under both readings.
named: a third-octave coefficient table indexed by the byte's high nibble

measurements.read_as: The width byte of the same section, swept with the frequency byte held at 64. It is the control on the reading and not evidence about the table: a byte that changes how wide a feature is and not where it sits must leave a reading of where it sits alone. The fitted position holds inside 0.024 octaves while the window it was fitted over runs from four bands to forty-nine, and the largest band moves 0.167 octaves over the same settings -- so what the bottom three entries disagree by is not the feature's width being read as its place.

document_rows.read_as: Evidence that a page prints those two figures against those two addresses, and nothing about the unit. What the claim takes from them is the two ends of the table and not any entry between them: every entry here is a named third octave, which is a reading of the series and is the part a reader may disagree with.

era_priors.claim: A frequency parameter of this period is a table of filter coefficients indexed by the byte, not a frequency the part computes coefficients from.
era_priors.why: Turning a frequency into a biquad needs a sine and a tangent, which a small control processor of the era would run once per parameter change and would rather not. Storing the coefficients instead makes the entry expensive in memory, which is why the table is short where a rate table is not: a rate entry is one number and a filter entry is a set.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: Two settings inside one entry returned different frequencies at a resolution the run can tell apart, or the number of distinct values across the byte turned out to be near a hundred and twenty-eight.

era_priors.claim: A table's stride is a power of two, because dividing by one is a shift.
era_priors.why: A hundred and twenty-eight settings over sixteen entries is eight each. A table of twenty entries would need a divide or a second table, which is the reason the printed range that holds twenty third octaves is expected to behave differently and is the run this claim queues.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: The entry boundaries turned out not to fall on multiples of eight -- which is measurable at settings 6, 7, 8 and 9 and has not been asked.

adds: Each record says which band the deviation was largest in at each setting it was asked at, and says in as many words that no filter, no corner and no order is in it. Nothing in either record says the readings are entries of a table, that the table has sixteen of them, that eight settings share one, or that the entries are the third octaves the page's two ends bracket. That is the whole of what is added here, and it is added by holding five candidate laws against the same readings rather than by fitting one to them.

alternatives.reading: The entries are sixteen frequencies at equal ratios between the printed ends rather than the named third octaves. On 200 - 6.3k the two differ by at most a third of a percent.

separated_by.observable: Where the entries of a printed range fall whose ends bracket a number of third octaves that is not sixteen.

predicts.the named third octaves: The entries are the series whatever the ends, so 100 - 8.0k holds twenty of them. Twenty entries cannot be reached by a stride of eight, so the stride is six and the last eight settings return the last entry -- which is the shape the rate table already turned out to have.
predicts.sixteen at equal ratios: The entries are recomputed from the ends, so 100 - 8.0k holds sixteen at 0.42 octaves apart, the stride stays eight, and none of the entries is a named third octave.

separated_by.divergence: 0.21 octaves at setting 72 and 0.27 at setting 96, on top of a stride of six against a stride of eight
separated_by.sensitivity_here: One twelfth-octave band, 0.083 octaves, which is what the run resolves a feature to

run.stimulus: A held note, as the equaliser sweeps used. This slot is a phaser's manual frequency and what it moves is a notch rather than a peak, so the run must hold the phaser's rate at its slowest first and the record has to say it did: a notch that is sweeping while the take runs averages to no notch at all.

alternatives.reading: The three entries are 200, 250 and 315 and the filter built from them does not peak there. A table entry of this period is a set of coefficients rather than a frequency, so what is stored is already the filter -- and a section whose response below 300 Hz is not the peaking biquad the model renders would put its top somewhere else while the entry behind it is exactly the named one.

separated_by.observable: Whether the fitted position moves with the width byte at the bottom of the frequency byte's range, where at the middle of it it does not.
separated_by.divergence: 0.15 octaves, which is how far below the named series the three low entries read and is what either answer has to account for
separated_by.sensitivity_here: One twelfth-octave band, 0.083 octaves. The floor is the band and not what a fit can do, because how far apart the same setting's own takes put a fitted position has not been measured anywhere in this archive -- so the run is queued against the figure that has been

predicts.the entry is where it is read: The fitted position holds within a few hundredths of an octave across the width byte's values, exactly as it does at setting 64, and stays near 179 Hz at all of them.
predicts.the section is not a biquad down there: The fitted position moves with the width byte by more than the band it is read against, because a response that is not symmetric in log frequency is read at a different place as its flanks change.

run.why_this_shape: The same sweep the width byte already has at data/units/roland-sc8850-01/efx-bands/01-00-08-where-the-eq-hinges-in-twelfths.json, with the frequency byte at 0 instead of 64. That record is the control this one is read against, so it is the one run that answers the question and nothing else has to be repeated. Only six settings because the byte answers to 0 through 4 and reads everything above as 0, which that record already showed.

alternatives.reading: The three entries below 315 Hz really are 200, 250 and 315 and the disagreement is the reading, not the table: the largest band of a peak this wide is a coarse estimator, and the peak's top is flat enough that a tenth of a decibel moves it.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: The reading it asked for was made and says the opposite. Located by a fit over the whole feature rather than by the largest band, the three entries read 179.2, 240.3 and 279.7 Hz against 200, 250 and 315 -- 0.06 to 0.17 octaves low, where the same reading puts every entry above them inside a fifth of a band of the model. It is not scatter in the fit: the other mid section, which shares nothing with this one but the table, reads 179.1 Hz at the same setting, and the same takes read at a third of an octave instead of a twelfth put the low group 0.13 octaves out rather than 0.15. It is not the feature's width being read as its place either: the width byte of this section moves the fitted position by 0.024 octaves across every value it answers to, while moving the window that position is fitted over from four bands to forty-nine.

alternatives.reading: Thirty-two entries at equal ratios, four settings each.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: It puts settings 0 and 4 in different entries and settings 8 and 12 in different entries. The reading tells neither pair apart, and the pairs are the settings the run asked precisely because four apart is where a finer table would show.

alternatives.reading: Eight entries at equal ratios, sixteen settings each.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: It puts settings 0 and 8 in one entry. The reading tells them apart by five bands.

alternatives.reading: No table: the printed ends of a ratio scale over all 128 settings.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: It gives every setting its own frequency, so settings 0 and 4 and settings 8 and 12 are all distinct. The reading tells neither pair apart. It is also two bands out at seven of the twelve settings, where the winner is exact.

alternatives.reading: No table: the printed ends of an evenly divided line in hertz.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: It is 1.75 octaves out in the middle of the byte, which is twenty-one bands.

refuted_by: Two settings inside one of these entries returning frequencies the run tells apart, or two settings across an entry boundary returning frequencies it does not. Either is measurable at settings 4 through 12 of any slot printed with a frequency range. Or a slot on the same printed range whose readings do not land on this series at all, which would make the table a property of the type rather than of the range.

compared_against.generated_from: data/units/roland-sc8850-01/index.json, filtered to the efx-bands records of type 01 00 whose swept address is a mid frequency byte, at the finest resolution published.

excluded.why: The null control, where the byte was swept with the gain it shapes at its centre. There is no feature to put anywhere, so there is no place to be right or wrong about. The record is still answered -- with nothing -- and that answer is a level and is scored as one.
The same, for the other mid section.

stimulus: A held note through the effect, its takes read as the energy of each twelfth octave against the run's own flat repeats.
domain.outside: Every printed frequency range except 200 - 6.3k, and every type except 01 00. The range that holds twenty third octaves rather than sixteen is the one this claim most expects to behave differently and it has not been measured. Which setting selects Bypass, on the fourteen ranges that print it. The two shelf corners of this same type, printed 200/400 and 4k/8k: a page's shelf frequency and a measurement of one are not defined at the same point, so those slots are not evidence here. The width of what sits at the frequency, which is a separate byte. Any setting between the twelve asked.

residual.unit: octaves between the band the model peaks in and the band the unit peaks in
residual.why: Zero at eight of the twelve settings and at two of the three at the other address: the model's peak falls in the identical band, not a near one. The residual leans because the four that are not zero are all at the bottom, one to two bands high, which is a structure and is reported as one rather than averaged away. The floor is one band, which is what the reading resolves. There is no second floor here: one entry of the table would be a coarser one and would swallow the disagreement, and that floor is only admissible where the stride has been measured -- on this class the stride is the question.

also_read_as.unit: octaves between where a fit puts the model's peak and where it puts the unit's
also_read_as.why: The same rendering and the same records, located by a fit over the whole feature instead of by the largest band, which is the run the claim queued and cost no hardware. Every figure moves and nothing about the finding does. The ranking is unchanged and the winner is unchanged; the winner's residual rises from zero to 0.038 octaves and the runner-up's falls from 0.125 to 0.091, so the two are 2.2 times apart rather than infinitely, which is the honest separation and the other was partly the band set rounding both to the same place. Above setting 32 the disagreement is 0.013 to 0.047 octaves. Below it, it is 0.056 to 0.171 -- the same breakdown, in the same place, at the same size.

gross.why: The median residual over the span the effect commands, taken as the worst of the records scored. A rejection bound and not a target: below it the residual is reported and never optimised, because no candidate is decided by it.

qualitative.why: Properties the unit's readings have that the model's readings must have too. No arithmetic over a residual rescues a model that cuts where the unit boosts.

power.beaten_by: contradicting a property the winner satisfies
power.why: The runner-up in the catalogue, scored on the same records, and whether it leans or contradicts a property where the winner does neither. The decoy is not chosen -- it is whichever candidate came second, so a strawman cannot be put up in its place. A class holding one candidate is a catalogue that is unfinished, which is a finding and not a pass.

breakdown.why: A point worse than 0.5 of the span is a failure at that point rather than error at it. A residual that leans with the setting or with frequency is pointing at a structure the model does not have; one that does not is pointing at the room and the converters, and is not made smaller by anything this project can do.

what_this_does_not_close.why: They read 0.06 to 0.17 octaves below where the named series puts them, at both addresses, at two band widths and under both readings of where a feature sits. That is the breakdown, it is why the verdict is not `reproduces`, and it is the second alternative above. What it is not is the reading: the run that would have shown that has been made and shows the opposite.
what_this_does_not_close.what_would: Whether the section is still a peaking biquad down there. Everything measured so far says the number belongs to the unit and not to the instrument -- two sections that share nothing but the table agree at setting 0 to 0.0008 octaves, the figure survives a fourfold change in band width, and the width byte moves the fitted position by 0.024 octaves while moving the window it is fitted over twelvefold. What is left is that a table entry of 200 Hz is right and the filter built from it does not peak at 200 Hz, which nothing here separates from an entry that is not 200 Hz. Sweeping the width byte with the frequency byte at 0 separates them: a fitted position that moves with the width is a section not behaving like a biquad, and one that holds is an entry that is where it is read.

what_this_does_not_close.what: The other thirty-four slots the page prints a frequency range against.
what_this_does_not_close.why: Six others are printed 200 - 6.3k, at five other types, and would be this same table if the printed range is what chooses it -- which is the whole of what `chosen_by` in the model asserts and none of it is measured. Twenty-eight are printed with other ends. One of those, 100 - 8.0k, brackets twenty third octaves, which a stride of eight cannot reach; six of the thirty-six slots carry it and every one of them is a phaser's manual frequency. None of the thirty-four has been measured.
what_this_does_not_close.what_would: One efx-bands sweep of a slot printed 100 - 8.0k at nine settings, which is the first alternative above and is queued. It answers two things at once: whether the entries are the named series, and whether a table that will not divide the byte by a power of two takes a stride of six and leaves the last eight settings on its last entry.

what_this_does_not_close.what: Whether the Q byte indexes its printed table the same way.
what_this_does_not_close.why: The page prints five values against it and the equaliser model fits five entries, which is the same shape. But the fitted entries are close to half the printed ones for four of the five and not for the fifth, which is a definition question about what Q means on each side rather than a table question, and it is not answered by anything here.
what_this_does_not_close.what_would: Nothing new to measure. The five entries were already read at every setting; what is missing is a statement of which bandwidth definition the printed figures are, and that is a reading of the page.

a_note_on_what_it_replaces: That claim's sentence already says a centre moves for every eighth value of its byte, and its model does not: the model carries the twelve settings the run asked and interpolates between them, which is the measurement wearing the clothes of a law. This is the same sentence held against a catalogue instead of asserted, and with the entries named. Nothing about the chain around it changes -- the model here is that model with one map swapped, so that the residual answers one question.
a_note_on_what_was_left_out: The first pass over this class scored the same five candidates as whole band profiles in decibels and returned `equivalent_under_this_test`: every candidate passed the gross gate and none leaned. That was not the candidates agreeing. Sliding a peak of this width by a sixth of an octave costs a decibel or two on its flanks and nothing at its top, so the residual in decibels stayed under the run's own floor for candidates that were two bands out at every setting -- and a residual that is the same size everywhere does not lean, so the gate that catches a wrong structure could not catch a wrong place either. The reading was changed, not the gate's threshold: where the feature sits is what the byte moves, and the record already published it. The reading it was changed to was then changed again, and this is the second half of the same lesson. The largest band is quantised to a band, so a peak halfway between two of them cannot be read closer than half a band however good the takes are, and on a broad feature a tenth of a decibel decides which of the two it is: the width byte above moves it two bands without moving the feature at all. A fit over the whole feature is not quantised and does not do that -- and it has a bias the largest band does not, because a symmetric curve fitted to a feature whose flanks are not symmetric tops out towards the longer one. Neither reading is the better one, which is why the record now publishes both, and why what was done here was to score the same candidates twice rather than to swap one reading for the other. The finding is what survived both.
